Users who regularly use ChatGPT for quick image searches can now add photos to conversations more quickly through a brand new gesture. Let's take a look at how to use it.

ChatGPT makes it easier for users to add just-taken photos to conversations

Although iOS's Visual Intelligence feature has been available for nearly two years, it currently only supports newer iPhone models and is not available in all regions.

For users who rely on ChatGPT for similar visual searches, previously adding an image required tapping the "+" button, selecting "Photos," and then choosing the appropriate image from the album.

Although the process wasn't exactly complicated, OpenAI simplified the steps slightly this week. Users can now add recently taken photos to conversations through a convenient new gesture.

OpenAI's Adam Fry said on the X platform that users can now long-press the "+" button on the left side of the input field to instantly bring up the four most recently taken photos.

Users can select a photo from there to add to the conversation, then ask questions or incorporate it into their prompt.

This new gesture is one of several improvements ChatGPT has made this week. Other updates include more accurate handling of the current time, improved loading and execution speed for long conversations on the web version, and providing clearer interface prompts when users are waiting for a network connection.

Have you ever tried using AI for visual searches? Feel free to share with us in the comments section.
